title: Thai PM Survives 4th No-Confidence Vote in Parliament
claim: Prayuth survived a no-confidence vote with 256 votes in favor and 206 against, after four days of public grilling over corruption and economic mismanagement.
source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting republished by VOA with precise vote totals and context on the coalition's parliamentary strength.
period_fit: Directly in 2022 and squarely within the ruler-period.
ruler_attribution: Strongly attributable to Prayut's coalition management and parliamentary control, though not proof of policy success.
contrary_evidence: The opposition framed the vote as about corruption and economic mismanagement.
Survival in parliament does not by itself show effective governance.

title: Opposition ups pressure on Prayut as coalition misses House quorum again
claim: The PPRP-led coalition failed to make quorum, adjourning the House for the 17th time, and the article describes the coalition as fragile and internally disunited.
source_confidence_reason: Local reporting with concrete parliamentary detail; less authoritative than Reuters but still specific and time-locked.
period_fit: Within the target year and directly about coalition functionality.
ruler_attribution: Attributable to Prayut's governing coalition and his ability to keep legislators aligned, though factional autonomy matters.
contrary_evidence: Attendance failure may reflect MPs' behavior rather than direct personal action by Prayut.
The article also notes the coalition and opposition both share responsibility for House dysfunction.

title: Prayuth, all other censured ministers survive no-confidence vote
claim: Prayuth and 10 ministers survived the censure motion, with 256 votes of confidence against 206 no-confidence votes, and the article says the coalition remained intact after the vote.
locator: opening paragraphs and vote tally section
source_confidence_reason: It reports a specific parliamentary result, but is a secondary local outlet with less authority than Reuters.
period_fit: Within 2022 and directly relevant to coalition control.
ruler_attribution: Attributable to Prayut's coalition discipline and parliamentary bargaining, with major influence from coalition partners.
contrary_evidence: The article explicitly says the vote was widely expected to be followed by a cabinet reshuffle or more bargaining.
Survival does not show strong execution in policy delivery.

title: Office of Permanent Secretary policy_plan page
publisher: Office of Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Public Health
claim: The page lists FY2022 quarterly performance and budget-spending reports (S งป.301/302), annual ministry performance reports, and the government performance report for Gen. Prayut's first year, showing an active monitoring and reporting framework for implementation.
locator: Year 2565 section of the policy-plan page
source_confidence_reason: Official ministry portal with explicit document list for FY2022 reporting and performance tracking.
period_fit: Directly within the 2022 budget/implementation cycle.
ruler_attribution: Attributed to Prayut's cabinet and the Public Health ministry; this supports implementation machinery rather than Prayut's personal authorship.
contrary_evidence: This is a reporting framework and document index, not a consolidated audit of delivery quality.
It does not by itself prove that implementation met targets.

title: รายงานประจำปี 2565 กระทรวงศึกษาธิการ
claim: The 2022 annual report says it summarizes major education results under the ministry's action plan, including national-security education, research and development, lifelong human development, disadvantaged persons, disabled people, elderly people, teacher capacity, environmental stewardship, and public administration.
source_confidence_reason: Official ministry page describing its 2022 annual report and the scope of implementation covered in it.
period_fit: Covers FY2022 implementation, published shortly after the target year.
ruler_attribution: Mixed attribution to Prayut's cabinet and the education ministry; this is stronger on implementation than on Prayut personally.
contrary_evidence: This is still a ministry summary, not a line-by-line execution audit.
The page does not isolate Prayut's unique contribution from broader bureaucratic execution.

title: Thailand: 2022 Article IV Consultation-Press Release; Staff Report; and Statement by the Executive Director for Thailand
claim: The IMF says Thailand's authorities had started to withdraw large pandemic-related support in FY2022, reducing fiscal stimulus by 1.2 percent of GDP versus FY2021, extending some energy-price measures through the fiscal year, and approving targeted cash transfers to vulnerable groups worth about 0.2 percent of GDP.
source_confidence_reason: Official IMF staff report with concrete fiscal-policy detail and a clear link to 2022 policy decisions.
period_fit: Directly addresses FY2022 policy adaptation within the target period.
ruler_attribution: Attributed to Thai authorities under Prayut's government; not all of the policy choice is uniquely personal to Prayut, but the cabinet clearly owned the response.
contrary_evidence: The report is partly forward-looking and advisory.
The IMF also notes that energy subsidies were still costly and regressive.

title: Thailand extends measures to tackle high oil prices, help tourism
claim: Thailand's cabinet extended energy-price support and tourism measures, including a 100-baht monthly cooking-gas subsidy for low-income earners, freezing vehicle gas prices for taxi drivers, and seeking refinery contributions to the oil fund; Prayut said fiscal discipline meant spending had to be sparse.
locator: Reuters dateline paragraphs in the article body
source_confidence_reason: Reuters contemporaneous reporting with specific cabinet actions and an exact date.
period_fit: Directly within 2022 and responsive to an inflation shock.
ruler_attribution: Cabinet action under Prayut; attribution is strong for the policy choice, weaker for any downstream effectiveness claim.
contrary_evidence: Temporary relief does not show long-term success.
The policy was a defensive response to external energy shocks rather than a structural reform.

title: Thai government spending to target low-income groups - Finance Minister
claim: Finance Minister Arkhom Termpittayapaisith said Thailand's stimulus would become more targeted toward vulnerable groups and low-income households as more people returned to work.
source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting of an explicit policy shift by the finance minister, contemporaneous and specific.
period_fit: Directly in 2022 and tied to the government's policy adjustment path.
ruler_attribution: Attributed to Prayut's finance and economic team; this is good evidence of course correction, though not uniquely Prayut's personal action.
contrary_evidence: The statement is a policy direction, not an implementation audit.
It does not prove the new targeting fully displaced broader support.
